module purpose: neorv32_cache is a direct-mapped cache between a host request/response port (host_req_i, host_rsp_o) and a system bus port (bus_req_o, bus_rsp_i): its controller (ctrl, lines 114-268) sends accesses at or above UC_BEGIN, atomic and debug accesses straight to the bus, serves read hits from the cache, writes write hits into the cache and through to the bus, downloads a whole block on a read miss, and clears the cache on a fence; the supplied sub-unit neorv32_cache_memory holds per-line valid bits, tags and data bytes and computes the hit signal (lines 366-428).

use-case flows.value: host access strobe and fence request, held in ctrl.buf_req and ctrl.buf_sync while the controller is busy and taken in S_IDLE
direct (uncached) access decision for addresses at or above UC_BEGIN, atomic and debug requests, and the pass-through of the bus response

lookup: tag and index captured from the request address, hit computed from the stored valid bit and tag, read hit answered from the cache, write hit written into the cache and through to the bus, misses sent to download or direct access
block download (refill): line allocated, words fetched from the bus at the stored tag, index and offset, written into the data memory, offset counted to the end of the block
bus error during a download: accumulated, refilled line invalidated, host answered with ack and err
cached data word returned to the host on a read hit
controller fields and all valid bits forced to zero / S_IDLE while rstn_i is low
fence-triggered clear of all valid bits (S_CLEAR, cmd_clr) and, when READ_ONLY is false, a fence driven to the bus

conceptual assets.concept: Cached data words -- the bytes held in the data memory and returned to the host on read hits
conceptual assets.reasoning: The refill and write-hit flows write bytes into the data memory: `data_mem_b0(to_integer(unsigned(acc_adr))) <= wdata_i(7 downto 0);` under `if (we_i(0) = '1')` (lines 413-414; bytes 1-3 at lines 416-423), fed by `cache_o.data <= bus_rsp_i.data;` during S_DOWNLOAD_RSP (line 236) or host data (line 151). The read-out flow returns them: `rdata_o( 7 downto 0) <= data_mem_b0(...)` (lines 425-428), wired to cache_i.data (line 291) and `host_rsp_o.data <= cache_i.data;` (line 156), acknowledged on a read hit (line 191). Integrity is Established: a read hit must return the bytes last written into that entry by the refill or write-hit flow. Availability is also Established: the bytes are held between writes and read on every clock edge (lines 412, 425-428). No line restricts who reads them, so confidentiality is not established. data_mem_b0-b3 store (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 2) and each SOURCES rdata_o, an output port of its entity (occurrence 3). rdata_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM data_mem_b0, occurrence 2), ahead of its own storage role. wdata_i sets: neorv32_cache_memory reads it to store the bytes (SOURCES data_mem_b0, occurrence 2). Not reported: cache_o.data only copies host_req_i.data or bus_rsp_i.data to the sub-unit (lines 151, 236, 290) and cache_i.data only carries rdata_o to host_rsp_o.data (line 156); neither is tested in a condition, so both are carriers. host_req_i, host_rsp_o, bus_req_o and bus_rsp_i are transport records (address, data, byte enables, strobe, ack, read data) and are excluded.

conceptual assets.reasoning: The controller defaults `cache_o.we <= (others => '0');` (line 150), sets `cache_o.we <= host_req_i.ben;` only in S_LOOKUP when ctrl.buf_dir is 0, cache_i.sta_hit is 1 and the access is a write (lines 186, 189, 190, 194), and sets `cache_o.we <= (others => '1');` in S_DOWNLOAD_RSP (line 237); a write miss goes to direct access without a cache write (lines 199-203). conceptual assets.concept: Cache hit decision -- whether the requested address is present and valid in the cache
conceptual assets.reasoning: The decision is computed by `hit_o <= '1' when (valid_mem_rd = '1') and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag) else '0';` (line 405) and wired to cache_i.sta_hit (line 286).
